html:
A wave of riots that swept across Japan from July to September 1918, set off by soaring rice prices. They were the largest popular uprising in modern Japanese history.

The price of rice, the staple food, more than doubled between 1917 and 1918. The boom of the First World War had raised prices, merchants hoarded, and the government was buying rice for troops it was about to send into Siberia. The trouble began in July in Uozu, a fishing town on the Sea of Japan, where fishermen's wives tried to stop rice being shipped out. Riots spread to cities, towns and mining districts across the country. Rioters attacked rice dealers and the homes of the rich.

The army restored order, and thousands were arrested. The prime minister Terauchi Masatake resigned, and in his place came Hara Takashi, the first head of a party cabinet and the first commoner prime minister. The riots pushed Japan toward a more party based politics in the 1920s and toward imports of rice from its colonies, Korea and Taiwan.
sum: A wave of riots that swept across Japan from July to September 1918, set off by soaring rice prices. They were the largest popular uprising in modern Japanese history.
